advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat an empty base_sha for the default base branch as an error (or otherwise guard it) rather than launching the workflow with base_sha=''.
evidence: intake_runtime.py:50-54: `base = start.base or self._settings.github_default_base_branch` ... `if start.base and not base_sha: raise UnresolvableBaseBranch(base, start.repo)` — the guard is gated on `start.base` being truthy
intake_runtime.py:26: `remote_head` returns '' when stdout is empty, i.e. the branch produced no ref
draft_pull_request.py:426: `repository_sha=params.base_sha` — an empty base_sha flows into the workflow
ABSENCE: test_start_falls_back_to_the_default_base_branch stubs remote_head to always return 'main-sha', so the empty-default-base case is never exercised (test_intake_runtime.py)
advisory.finding: The base-SHA existence guard is applied only to declared base branches: `if start.base and not base_sha` skips validation when the default base branch is used. If `remote_head` returns '' for the default branch (branch absent on remote), no error is raised and the workflow starts with base_sha='' — a silent fail-open indistinguishable from a successful resolution.
scenarios: github_default_base_branch is misconfigured or the branch does not exist on a given repo; a ticket carries no base: label.

test_start_falls_back_to_the_default_base_branch sets `remote_head` -> "main-sha" (non-empty), so the empty-default path never runs
ABSENCE: no test invokes start(_intake_start()) (base unset) with `remote_head` returning "" to assert no raise; a regression flipping the guard to `if not base_sha:` would go undetected
advisory.finding: The newly-added guard `if start.base and not base_sha:` is not tested for the default-base case where the resolved sha is empty; no test drives base="" with remote_head returning "" to confirm the guard does NOT raise UnresolvableBaseBranch for an undeclared/default base.
scenarios: Default branch does not resolve on the remote and base is undeclared: current code proceeds (base_sha="") without raising; a regression removing the `start.base and` guard would raise instead, unnoticed by tests
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: monkeypatch remote_head -> "", call starter.start(_intake_start()) (no base), assert it does not raise and arg.base_sha == "".

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Prevent per-pass re-seeding/re-snapshotting when a declared base branch is unresolvable (e.g. validate the base before seeding, or record the failed intake_start so it is not retried on every pass).
evidence: intake_reconciler.py:361: `await ctx.execution_seeder.seed(execution_id=execution_id, task_id=issue_key, repo=repo)` runs inside `_launch` before `ctx.starter.start(...)` at line 379
intake_reconciler.py:395-399: `try: outcome = await ctx.ledger.run_once(ref, _launch) except UnresolvableBaseBranch as exc: await _hold(...)`

idempotency.py:81-95: `reserve` inserts a _PENDING row and only returns replayed=True when `existing.status == _COMPLETED`; a raised effect never reaches `record()` so the key remains _PENDING and re-runs next pass
intake_runtime.py:53-54: `if start.base and not base_sha: raise UnresolvableBaseBranch(base, start.repo)` is raised from inside the starter, i.e. after seed/snapshot
blocking.finding: When a declared base branch is unresolvable, UnresolvableBaseBranch is raised inside `_launch`, which has already seeded a new execution_id and captured a task snapshot before the starter raises. Because the exception propagates out of `ledger.run_once` before `record()` runs, the `intake_start` side-effect key stays _PENDING (only _COMPLETED counts as replayed), so each subsequent reconcile pass re-runs `_launch`, seeding a fresh execution and capturing another snapshot for as long as the branch remains unresolvable.
scenarios: A ticket declares base:<branch> that does not (yet) exist on the remote; the intake reconciler runs repeatedly on a schedule.
